description: This checklist is used to audit the JSON page definition files within the implement-modules/question-to-user/v5/ module. Each page should be checked against these criteria to ensure consistency, correctness, and adherence to project standards as outlined in docs/ROOT.md.

items.text: Valid JSON: The file is a valid JSON document.
Schema Conformance: The JSON structure conforms to the project's page schema (e.g., as per docs/ui/json-template-schema.md or other relevant page structure standards).
Root Element: The page has a defined root element or layout structure.
Comments: All comments (if any, e.g., // end-of-line) are correctly formatted and do not break JSON parsing (assuming a pre-processor handles comments as per project rules).
Component Mapping: All component types used are defined in component-map.json (or equivalent mapping mechanism).
PrimeVue Wrappers: Components are used via their established PrimeVue wrappers (e.g., Button.vue, Card.vue).
Props Validity: All component props are valid for the respective components and correctly typed (string, boolean, number, object, array).
Props Naming: Props follow consistent naming conventions.
Required Props: All required props for components are provided.
Text Content: All static text content (labels, titles, placeholders) is clear, concise, and free of typos.
Localization: Text content is prepared for localization if applicable (e.g., using keys or specific structures).
Data Binding: Dynamic data bindings are correctly configured.
Placeholder Content: No placeholder or lorem ipsum text remains in production-ready definitions.
Client-Side Actions (`customHooks`): `customHooks` are correctly defined and target existing client-side logic as per docs/ui/core-concepts/module-actions.md.
Server-Side Actions (`instructions`): Server-side actions are correctly defined as per docs/ui/commands-and-operations/server-actions-reference.md.
Event Handling: Event handlers are correctly defined and associated with appropriate components.
Component Reusability: Common UI patterns are implemented using reusable components/sub-schemas where possible.
Self-Contained: The page definition is reasonably self-contained or clearly defines its dependencies.
ARIA Labels: Components have `aria-label` or equivalent for non-textual elements where appropriate.
Keyboard Navigation: Interactive elements are keyboard accessible (inherent from PrimeVue, but verify custom interactions).
Focus Management: Basic focus management is considered (inherent from PrimeVue).
File Naming: The JSON page file itself follows project naming conventions.
Internal IDs/Keys: IDs or keys used within the JSON (e.g., for elements, actions) are unique and follow conventions.
UI Consistency: The page maintains UI consistency with other pages in the module and project.
Page Purpose: The purpose of the page is clear either from its name, content, or associated documentation.
In-File Metadata: Any required metadata within the JSON (e.g., version, author, description fields) is present and correct.
Backend-Driven UI: The page definition aligns with the backend-driven UI principle.
Separation of Concerns: The page definition focuses on UI structure and presentation, not business logic.

auditProcessNotes: For each item, the 'status' can be 'Pass', 'Fail', or 'N/A'. Document any 'Fail' items with details and proposed fixes in a separate audit log or notes section.
